text:
Fixed and verified. Found a second false-certainty path the review did not name.

RED first, both new tests failing against the parent commit:
1. exit 255 + "module: command not found" + writeCompleted=true => AgentUnavailable (write flag discarded).
2. exit 255 + "cat: /scratch/secret: Permission denied" + writeCompleted=true => AuthenticationFailed (write flag discarded).

The second was NOT in the bead. authenticationMarker matched a bare "permission denied", so a remote program reporting an inaccessible FILE was classified as OpenSSH authentication failure — the same class of defect as the "not found" match, reached by a different route, with the same consequence: AuthenticationFailed carries no write flag, so the scheduler adapter reports a definite "never submitted" for a job that may be queued.

Fix (SshAgentWireClient.scala:139, :152):
- Agent absence restricted to exit 126 (found but not executable) and 127 (not found). These are the only exits that PROVE the agent never ran, which is why discarding the write flag is sound there and nowhere else.
- Authentication markers narrowed to OpenSSH-shaped diagnostics: "permission denied (", "permission denied, please try again", "too many authentication failures", "no supported authentication methods available". Bare "permission denied" and bare "authentication failed" were dropped.

Design bias worth recording: where the message is ambiguous, classification now falls through to TransportDisconnected, which PRESERVES uncertainty rather than asserting a cause. Losing an authentication classification costs a slightly vaguer diagnostic; losing the write flag costs a false "never submitted". Those are not symmetric, so ambiguity resolves toward the transport case.

CORRECTION TO THE REVIEW, confirmed: the write flag is NOT misnamed. requestWriteCompleted (SshProcessRunner.scala:35), writeCompleted (:83) and afterRequestWrite (AgentProtocol.scala:148) all honestly say "write", the write is genuinely local (:165), and no doc claims remote receipt. Nothing was renamed.

The bead also asked to carry the write flag on every AgentFailure variant reachable post-write. Deliberately NOT done, because it is unnecessary once classification is correct: RemoteCliFailure, RemoteAgentFailure, ProtocolViolation and ProtocolMismatch all arise only AFTER a successful exchange (SshAgentWireClient.scala:103-126), so delivery is implied rather than lost; and AgentUnavailable/AuthenticationFailed are now reachable only where the request demonstrably was not processed. Widening the ADT would have added six fields carrying information already implied by the variant, and P8.D5 is about to replace this ADT with CallFailure anyway.

Verification: 3 new tests (2 RED-proven plus an exit-126 regression guard). Full suite 322, 0 failed. scalafmt clean.
